review_type: independent intermediate implementation security and privacy review
summary: Three reproduced Apple integration defects require changes: relay-disable metadata does not govern email authority, notification revocation produces a state rejected by the methods contract and fresh-consent login, and completed account purge retains known-account notification fingerprints. Existing bounded tests pass; this is an intermediate code review and makes no delivery, live-provider or device acceptance claim.

findings.category: Apple relay delivery and email authority
findings.title: Use the same relay-disabled flag in notification and email eligibility
findings.description: A validated email-disabled notice writes email_delivery_disabled, but _email_usable checks email_disabled. The account therefore continues to advertise and enqueue this relay address for email login, recovery and reauthentication. The synthetic transport acknowledged a new post-notice code, and verification returned signed_in. This is an integration defect; the reproduction does not claim that a disabled live Apple relay will deliver mail or that account takeover was demonstrated.
findings.requirement: FR-025 and accepted HTTP/data-model relay events affect only the matching relay destination and make its delivery method unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Unify the persisted metadata flag and its readers. Add an integration regression from a verified matching relay notice through account methods and each email-purpose eligibility decision, including email-enabled restoration and nonmatching-address isolation.

findings.title: Reconcile revoked bindings with the response schema and fresh-consent transition
findings.description: A validated consent-revoked/account-deleted notice sets state='revoked'. Account methods passes that value to ConnectedMethod, whose allowed states are active/disabled, producing a Pydantic literal_error for a surviving password session and an unhandled route failure. Fresh explicit Apple login also fails: completion reactivates only disabled bindings, then record_grant rejects revoked bindings. An assertion issued one second after the revocation was rejected and the binding stayed revoked. This prevents the accepted fresh-consent recovery/reconnection path and can strand an account whose remaining configured method is Apple.
findings.requirement: FR-025, the active/disabled connected-method contract, and accepted strictly newer explicit consent/generation handling.
findings.recommendation: Define one consistent persisted/public state transition. Preserve revocation of old sessions/proofs, require strictly newer valid Apple consent before restoration, increment the generation atomically, and make login/link plus account-method responses cover revocation without schema failure. Add service/API integration regressions rather than manually resetting state in lifecycle-only tests.

findings.title: Remove or anonymize known-account Apple receipts during final purge
findings.description: Notification receipts for a known binding retain an unkeyed subject fingerprint, generation and event times. The table has no owner foreign key, delete_for_user omits it, and final user deletion cannot cascade to it. A full AccountService.purge_account reproduction removed the user and bindings but left both known-account receipts unchanged (2 before, 2 after, users=0). These fingerprints remain correlatable to the provider subject in the owner's export until the eight-day receipt TTL. The TTL is bounded, but the accepted erasure exception names unknown/public abuse fingerprints; it does not authorize retaining known-account personal metadata after final purge.
findings.requirement: FR-018/SC-005 and data-model export/erasure: final purge removes all account-owned new records/jobs; unknown/public abuse fingerprints may expire on their bounded schedule.
findings.recommendation: Associate known-binding receipts with their owner for purge, or erase their subject/generation linkage at purge while retaining only a content-free global replay tombstone if needed. Verify complete purge and idempotent retry separately from unknown-subject receipt expiry.

verification.name: synthetic_apple_integration_reproductions
verification.fixture_boundary: Temporary local database; existing conftest container; fake provider verification/exchange and mail transport; synthetic generated P-256 key. This tests post-verification lifecycle integration, not live signature/provider/device behavior.
verification.stdin:
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
import pytest
from pydantic import SecretStr, ValidationError
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from tests import conftest
from tests.test_modern_auth_service import make_modern, request, verify, challenge, VERIFIER
from tests.test_auth_apple_lifecycle import Gateway, APPLE
from app.services.auth_apple_lifecycle import AuthAppleLifecycle
from app.services.auth_provider_service import AppleNotification, ProviderIdentity, ProviderTokens
from app.schemas.modern_auth import ProviderStartRequest, ProviderCompleteRequest

with TemporaryDirectory(prefix='auth-security-review-') as directory:
    data = Path(directory) / 'data'
    data.mkdir()
    mp = pytest.MonkeyPatch()
    cg = conftest.container.__wrapped__(data, mp)
    container = next(cg)
    try:
        service, mail, sent, provider, clock = make_modern(container)
        owner = container.auth_service.seed_admin(email='relay@example.com', password='synthetic-long-password')
        owner = container.user_repo.mutate(owner.id, lambda user: user.model_copy(update={'email_verified_at':clock()}))
        _, token, _ = container.auth_service.login(email=owner.email, password='synthetic-long-password')
        created = (clock() - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
        with service.store.transaction() as c:
            c.execute('INSERT INTO auth_identity_bindings(id,user_id,provider,issuer,namespace,subject,created_at,updated_at,email,is_private_email) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,1)', ('apple-binding', owner.id, 'apple', APPLE, 'brainbuddy', 'apple-subject', created, clock().isoformat(), owner.email))
        gateway = Gateway()
        lifecycle = AuthAppleLifecycle(service.store, service.box, gateway, clock=clock)
        service.apple = lifecycle
        event_time = int(clock().timestamp())
        gateway.notification = AppleNotification('delivery-review', 'email-disabled', 'apple-subject', 'com.example.web', event_time, event_time, owner.email, True)
        lifecycle.process_notification('signed synthetic fixture')
        print('repro_disabled_relay_email_stays_usable:', service._email_usable(owner))
        pending = request(service, owner.email)
        mail.dispatch_one()
        result = verify(service, pending.challenge_id, sent[-1][1])
        print('repro_disabled_relay_login_result:', result.payload.status)
        gateway.notification = AppleNotification('revocation-review', 'consent-revoked', 'apple-subject', 'com.example.web', event_time, event_time)
        lifecycle.process_notification('signed synthetic fixture')
        try:
            service.account_methods(raw_token=token)
            print('repro_revoked_binding_breaks_account_methods: unexpectedly accepted')
        except ValidationError as error:
            print('repro_revoked_binding_breaks_account_methods:', [(e['loc'], e['type']) for e in error.errors(include_input=False)])
        clock.now += timedelta(seconds=1)
        key = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1()).private_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM, serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8, serialization.NoEncryption()).decode()
        service.settings = service.settings.model_copy(update={'apple_team_id':'ABCDEFGHIJ','apple_key_id':'KLMNOPQRST','apple_private_key':SecretStr(key),'apple_services_id':'com.example.web','apple_native_app_id':'com.example.native'})
        identity = ProviderIdentity('apple', APPLE, 'apple-subject', owner.email, True, True, 'com.example.web', int(clock().timestamp()))
        provider.exchange_apple = lambda _code, **_kw: ProviderTokens(identity, 'com.example.web', SecretStr('synthetic-refresh'), 'refresh_token')
        started = service.start_provider('apple', ProviderStartRequest(purpose='login', client='web', client_challenge=challenge()))
        returned = service.provider_callback('apple', code='synthetic-code', state=started.payload.state, binder=started.binder)
        parameters = parse_qs(urlsplit(returned.url).fragment)
        try:
            result = service.complete_provider(ProviderCompleteRequest(attempt_id=parameters['attempt'][0], state=parameters['state'][0], handoff_code=parameters['grant'][0], client_verifier=VERIFIER))
            print('repro_fresh_apple_login_after_revocation:', result.payload.status)
        except Exception as error:
            print('repro_fresh_apple_login_after_revocation:', type(error).__name__)
        with service.store.connection() as c:
            print('repro_binding_state_after_fresh_apple_login:', c.execute('SELECT state FROM auth_identity_bindings WHERE id=?', ('apple-binding',)).fetchone()['state'])
            before = c.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM auth_apple_notification_receipts').fetchone()[0]
        container.account_service.purge_account(owner.id)
        with service.store.connection() as c:
            print('repro_notification_receipts_after_complete_purge:', {'before':before, 'after':c.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM auth_apple_notification_receipts').fetchone()[0], 'users':c.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users').fetchone()[0]})
    finally:
        try:
            next(cg)
        except StopIteration:
            pass
        mp.undo()
